Football.title: Roy Hodgson, 78, reveals body transformation that means he’s fitter than ever as he returns to Bristol City
Football.content:
ROY HODGSON has revealed that he lost “five or six kilos” while out of work.

The veteran boss, 78, made a surprise return to the dugout this week as he took the Bristol City job.





Hodgson replaced sacked Gerhard Struber at Ashton Gate, marking his return to management following more than two years out of the game.

The former England manager stepped down at Crystal Palace in February 2024 after collapsing during a training session.

During his unveiling as Bristol City boss, Hodgson made assurances over his health, claiming that he is: “Probably fitter now than I was when I left Crystal Palace.”

On his fitness regime, he added: “I’m lighter, about five or six kilos lighter, for a start.

“I’ve done a lot of work, having time on my hands – I’ve got a gym in our apartment, so I’ve done a lot of walking.”

Asked about what happened during his final Palace training session, Hodgson revealed: “I watched for another few minutes, then said, ‘No, I’ve got to go in, I don’t feel good’ – then I collapsed.

“Suddenly, you’ve got a load of people around you, the doctors come flying out. They made it feel like it isn’t good.

“They put me in the best clinic in London, a day and a half, every single test you’ve ever had, the most vigorous cardiac testing I’ve ever had. But the good thing is it was OK.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Hodgson has taken charge of Bristol City with the Robins winless in six.

He will oversee their last seven matches of the season, but has ruled out carrying on into next term.

Asked about the possibility, Hodgson smirked as he said: “No… I’m too old.”



The experienced operator returns to Ashton Gate 44 years after his last spell as Bristol City manager.

He’ll hope to perform better this time around, having won just three of his 21 matches in at the helm in 1982, in what was just the second of his 24 jobs in management.

Hodgson will kick off his return with a trip to Charlton on Friday.

Football.title: Former Arsenal star switches international allegiance weeks before World Cup despite playing three games for country
Football.content:
FORMER Arsenal talent Marcelo Flores has made the shock decision to switch his international allegiance to Canada in a last-ditch bid to save his World Cup dream.

The winger, 22, won three caps for Mexico when he was dubbed a teenage sensation.





But Flores is now pushing to feature at the World Cup with Canada, who are bossed by former Leeds chief Jesse Marsch.

The Tigres star came off the bench as a second half sub during a 2-2 draw with Iceland on Saturday.

It was Flores’ first call-up since failing to make it off the bench AGAINST Canada when he was in Mexico’s plans in September 2024.

And now he has put himself in a strong position to be involved in the summer extravaganza on home soil.

Flores donned the colours of Mexico at youth level and during the early stages of his international career after qualifying to represent the country because of his mother, despite being born in Canada.

He joined Arsenal from Ipswich in 2019, with the North Londoners fighting off competition from Barcelona, Manchester City and Chelsea.

But Flores walked away from the Emirates Stadium without ever being handed his senior debut.

And he was only named in the matchday squad by boss Mikel Arteta ONCE – when Arsenal suffered a 3-0 thumping against Crystal Palace in April 2022.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Flores sealed a switch to Mexican side Tigres in 2023 and has gone on to notch four goals in 17 appearances this season.

Canada’s World Cup campaign will get underway with a clash against Bosnia and Herzegovina or Italy.

They are going head-to-head tonight for a last-gasp spot in the tournament after seeing off Wales and Northern Ireland respectively in the play-off semi-finals.



Marsch’s side are then set to take on 2022 hosts Qatar in Vancouver on June 18.

And Canada’s final World Cup group stage meeting will see them face Switzerland six days later.

Former Arsenal youth player Marcelo Flores made his debut for Canada against Iceland. He previously plays three games for Mexico.

Football.title: ‘Ultimate football sacrifice’ – Scottish footie club reveals it’s folding because they’ve been TOO SUCCESSFUL
Football.content:
A SCOTTISH football club has announced it is being wound up – because they’ve been TOO SUCCESSFUL.

The decision comes on the back of three consecutive promotions and a flurry of cup wins over the last few years.



Fans of the team have expressed their disappointment at the news but the club has still been praised for what is being called “the ultimate football sacrifice”.



The town of Bo’ness near Falkirk is home to around just 15,000 people and until the end of this season, two senior football clubs.

Bo’ness United has been on the go for over 80 years and has three Scottish Junior Cups to its name.

The BU’s moved from the junior ranks to the East of Scotland Football League in 2018 and their success continued, winning promotion to the Lowland League and gaining SFA membership in 2020.

United’s departure from the junior leagues left a void many in the town felt needed filled.



And so Bo’ness Athletic was formed.

Bo’ness Athletic actually began back in 2001 as Linlithgow Thistle.

But they relocated to Bo’ness’ Newtown Park in 2019, with a kit and badge that closely resembled the town’s historical team.

OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

Initially, the two clubs were informal partners with one operating in the junior ranks and the other in the senior leagues.



But in 2021 all the remaining clubs in the East Region Juniors south of the River Tay decided to move to the East of Scotland Football League.

United were fearful of the impact another senior team in Bo’ness could have but such was the gap in the divisions they played in – and the fact they were ground sharing – they still weren’t really in direct competition with one another.

However as United established themselves in the Lowland League, Athletic began a rapid rise up through the lower ranks.

Athletic won the East of Scotland League’s Third Division (the ninth tier in Scottish football) in 2022-23, losing just ONCE in the league that season.

They also won the League Cup by defeating five opponents from higher divisions along the way.



Athletic then won the Second Division the following year and last season they were promoted once again, this time as runners-up in the First Division.

In that time they also won the Alex Jack Cup, the Cup Winners’ Shield and the King Cup.

At the moment Bo’ness Athletic sit sixth in the Premier Division while Bo’ness United sit eighth in the Lowland League (and will almost certainly transfer to the new Lowland League East next season).

It means now there’s just one division between the two Bo’ness clubs and with the upcoming restructuring due to take place in the Lowland League, a real prospect of them meeting in the near future.

And that has proved to be the tipping point.



Athletic say they can no longer continue with their “upward trajectory” as the town of Bo’ness should unite behind one team and one team only.

In a statement, the Bo’ness Athletic board said: “The Board of Bo’ness Athletic Football Club today announces the decision to formally wind up the club at the end of the season.

“Founded on the principle of providing a fresh footballing pathway within the town of Bo’ness, Bo’ness Athletic quickly grew into a competitive, progressive and ambitious side within the Scottish non-league structure.

“From its inception, the club sought not only to develop talent but also to contribute positively to the town’s proud footballing heritage.

“The club’s progress in recent seasons has been marked by strong performances, continuous progress, and increasing recognition across the game – with three successive promotions and six trophies, Scottish FA Licence and participation in the Scottish Cup.



“This upward trajectory has, however, coincided with ongoing structural changes within the Scottish football pyramid.

“As a result of these developments, the club faces a realistic prospect of progression beyond the East of Scotland Football League in the upcoming seasons.

“After thorough and careful consideration, and stagnating not an option, the committee concluded that such advancement would place the club in direct competition with the town’s established senior side with a long and distinguished history.

“In the interests of preserving unity within the local football community and avoiding duplication at senior level, the decision has been taken to wind up Bo’ness Athletic Football Club.

“The committee wishes to place on record its sincere gratitude to all players, management, coaching staff, volunteers, sponsors, and supporters who have contributed to the club’s success.



“Thanks are extended to the clubs and Board of the East of Scotland Football League, for which friendships have been established for life.

“Everyone’s efforts have ensured that Bo’ness Athletic leaves behind a proud and positive legacy not only in Bo’ness but across the country.”

Chairman Alex Brown and secretary Derek Oliver said the decision was a tough one to take but was done so to avoid the two clubs potentially vying for the same players and fans, maybe even leading to a future feud.

They said: “This has not been an easy decision. The club has been built on passion, commitment, and community spirit, and its achievements will remain a source of pride for all involved. We are immensely proud of what has been achieved in such a short space of time, both on and off the pitch.

“However, we believe that the long-term interests of football in Bo’ness are best served by maintaining a single senior pathway within the town. Bo’ness Athletic has been a success story, and that is something nobody can take away.”



Supporters on social media reacted with a mixture of shock, sadness and sympathy.

One said: “Tremendous achievement to take an amateur side through the ranks. Hopefully the experienced gained isn’t lost to the community.”

Another fan said: “Absolutely loved being involved from the start watching this club on a rocket powered rollercoaster… really gutted by the news, but what a journey and team, a great group of people.”

A third said: “Sad news! Fantastic achievement and came a long way from Linlithgow Thistle days.”

While this emotional fan said: “So sorry to read about the club finishing up but fully understand the reasoning. The joy this club has given me over the last four years is out of this world. The memories you have given me will never be forgotten. Let’s finish the season with a bang.”



Another neutral observer said: “Such a shame but totally understandable for the reasons given. We have enjoyed coming to watch Bo’ness Athletic on many occasions. Seen some absolute crackers of matches. Always been made really welcome by everyone at the club and also had the pleasure of seeing you lift a good few of the trophies you have won.

“All the best to all associated with the club.”

Another punter said: “Pretty incredible (and admirable) stuff from Bo’ness Athletic.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

While this fan said: “It’s the ultimate footballing sacrifice. I don’t think I have ever seen anything like it.”

Football.title: Eddie Howe’s future thrown into doubt as Newcastle chief reveals talks with under-fire boss after Sunderland disaster
Football.content:
EDDIE HOWE’s future as Newcastle boss will be thrashed out in the summer after a season of under-achievement at St James’ Park.

CEO David Hopkinson held talks with Howe last week in the wake of the Toon’s derby disaster at the hands of Sunderland.





Howe and his players were booed after that 2-1 defeat and for the first time since the Saudi takeover, fans are openly questioning the direction of the club.

And Hopkinson remains open-minded, suggesting all options are on the table.

He said of Howe’s position: “I don’t have a stance on his future. What I can tell you is the derby loss hurt and we take it seriously.

“There’s nothing within us that thinks ‘well, it’s just three points and on we go.’ It has resonated.



“I had a couple of hours in a one-on-one lunch recently with Eddie and we talked through a multitude of things, including that.

“Eddie’s our manager and I expect to have a great run to the end of the season and we’ll talk about the future when it’s time.”

Pressed to slam the door shut on talk of Howe leaving, he added: “We are not looking to make a change at the moment.

“We are not having those conversations. Right now, we are focused on the seven matches we have remaining and not distracting ourselves with speculation about what we may or may not do in the summer.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Whatever Howe’s fate, it promises to be a summer of change at Newcastle with Hopkinson paving the way for comings and goings.

Admitting for the first time that Alexander Isak’s acrimonious exit last August had been “a good sale” for the club, he claimed that in the present climate, Newcastle has evolved from a buying club into a trading model.

And that could see Sandro Tonali and other senior figures move on – particularly if, as seems likely, the Geordies miss out on Champions League qualification.



He said: “We think through what players might or might not want to do this summer.

“But if an Isak-like scenario presents itself again, any player under contract is going to leave on our terms and we’re going to maximise the opportunity that might represent for the club.

“Going forward, our strategy is to buy well and sell well.”

Asked if that meant cashing in on one of their prize assets, the Canadian added: “We’re not ready to answer that. We’ve got to see what set-up we’re in and what opportunities present themselves in the market place.

“What I will say is that we intend to be disciplined, active, thoughtful and as proactive as we possibly can but what’s the outcome going to be?



“I couldn’t begin to tell you.”

The club’s latest accounts for the year ending June 2025 reveal turnover increased by £15m to £335.3m with profit after tax rising to £34.7m.

Newcastle, however, are still lagging behind the Premier League elite in terms of financial muscle, but Hopkinson reiterated his claim that the club can be one of the world’s biggest by 2030.

He added: “They’ve got a headstart on us and we’ve got to catch these guys.



“We’ve got a tremendous opportunity for growth right in front of us.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The report also revealed Newcastle have sold St James’ Park – effectively to themselves in an overhaul of the club’s property holdings.

While an announcement on a move away from their existing ground or its redevelopment is not imminent, chief financial officer Si Capper said the reorganisation would give the club the financial headroom for future stadium plans.

Football.title: Marc Cucurella fumes Chelsea should never have sacked Enzo Maresca and admits players would ‘die for him’
Football.content:
MARC CUCURELLA says Chelsea should not have sacked Enzo Maresca in January, becoming the second player to call out the decision in recent weeks.

The Blues defender also said the club’s transfer policy is harming their chance of success in a scathing assessment of the ownership.





Maresca guided Chelsea to Europa Conference League and Club World Cup glory last year, but following a tense few months with the board – having repeatedly been denied defensive reinforcements – found himself out of a job.

Liam Rosenior was appointed as the next manager after joining from BlueCo sister club Strasbourg, but the team have entered the international break losing four games in a row, including an 8-2 collapse in the Champions League against Paris Saint-Germain.

In an interview with The Athletic, Cucurella defended Rosenior, but also said that Maresca should not have been sacked and the players would have died for their former manager.

The former Brighton man, whose contract was extended last year, blamed the instability at Chelsea on the ownership taking decisions that are unpopular with the players.

He said: “We knew what Maresca wanted from us. Winning a title like the Club World Cup also helps, strengthens the bond, and you create great relationships during the celebrations.

“When a manager gives you that confidence and offers you a platform to fight for titles, you’d die for him.

“The moment Maresca left, it had a big impact on us. These are decisions taken by the club. If you asked me, I would not have made this decision.

“To make a change like that, the best thing is to wait until the end of the season. You would give everyone, the players and the new manager, time to get ready, have a full pre-season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The instability around the club comes from this, in a nutshell.

“We had a caretaker first, then a new manager, with new ideas and no time to work on them. It is what it is.”

On the club’s transfer policy, Cucurella explained a number of players were “discouraged” after their humbling defeat to PSG, blaming it on a lack of experience.

The Spain international added that the policy of only signing young players might “complicate” the club’s ambition of winning serious silverware.

He added: “Results like that are always hard to take.



“You are fighting and training every day only to realise, at the very end, that when games matter, we are still a bit away from the top level.

“I understand this is part of the club’s policy, and that they want to take this direction — signing young players and looking to the future.

“But, for all of us who are still here and want to win big things, moments like this make you feel discouraged.

“We have a good core of players. The foundations are there. But to fight for major trophies such as the Premier League or the Champions League, you need more.

“Signing young players only might complicate achieving those goals. Against PSG, we lacked players that had gone through situations like that.



“You need time as well, and I know the young players are the ones that will have the experience in the future. But you need to find the balance between both worlds.”

He continued: “We lacked experience. For a lot of players, it was the first time playing a match of that calibre, and we paid the price.

“You can always make a mistake, but we should have handled it better. There was a return game to play, and if you keep a cool head, you go back to London with a 3-2 defeat and anything can happen.

“We made a mistake, tried to attack without a clear structure and then PSG took the chance and proved they have that cutting edge.”

Cucurella also suggested that Willie Isa, the former rugby league player who is now Chelsea’s player support and development officer, is in post effectively to make up for their lack of experience.



He added: “It is a thing that all the players decided to do before the games, following the advice from a coach.

“We have a coach in the backroom staff that helps us to be better from the mental side, too.

“As we lack profiles of experienced players, he gives us tips to project the image of a better team.”

Football.title: Ex-Premier League star on brink of one of the greatest ever escapes as he rescues strugglers from being 11 points adrift
Football.content:
ROB ELLIOT has overseen an incredible turnaround at Gateshead.

The former Newcastle star, 39, returned to the Heed in early January having previously bossed them during between 2023 and 2024.



Elliot previously replaced ex-Toon team-mate Mike Williamson at his old club’s National League neighbours.



During his first stint he led Gateshead to a sixth-place finish before achieving Wembley glory by winning the FA Trophy.

His exploits didn’t go unnoticed and in October 2024 he landed a two-and-a-half year deal at League One Crawley.

Following just six wins in 33 matches, however, Elliot was given the boot and the Sussex side went on to be relegated.

The ex-goalkeeper would return to work at Gateshead on January 2, greeted by a very different landscape to the one that he had left just 15 months earlier.

Elliot’s successor Carl Magnay left the club having missed out on a play-off place last season and was replaced by the club’s Under-19 coach Alun Armstrong.

The first half of the campaign was a disaster, however, with Armstrong shuffled into a head of football development role following a grim run of 11 matches without a win in all competitions.

In stepped Elliot, cast into a new role as firefighter with the Heed bottom of the National League.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The four-cap Ireland international did not have the instant impact that was desired.

Elliot lost his first five matches back at the helm, with his side looking doomed following a 2-1 home defeat to Brackley on February 14, their 13th in a row in the league.

But sometimes in football, it only takes one win to breathe life into a team.

And it was on February 17, in front of just 870 fans at The Shay, that Gateshead began their turnaround at Halifax.



Goals by Kenton Richardson and Mark Beck saw the Heed take a two-goal lead away from home, with Elliot’s men going on to win 2-1 despite Angelo Cappello’s second half goal for the hosts.

Elliot vowed that night: “We’ve got to use this as a springboard to push on now. We have to take this momentum forward.

“Forget everyone else and what they think. They’re writing us off, but I don’t care.

“I’m so pleased for the fans, it’s been a tough few months. Sometimes winning a game of football can make everyone feel good.”

A springboard it proved to be, with another win following that weekend at fellow strugglers Truro before an epic 4-4 draw with Morecambe, a match in which Gateshead were 3-1 down.



Since that Valentine’s Day defeat to Brackley, Gateshead have lost just two of 12 games.

On March 24 they produced arguably their best win yet, beating York 3-1 to cost the promotion hopefuls top spot.

A subsequent 2-1 triumph over Yeovil saw Elliot’s men climb five points above the drop zone with five games remaining, 21st place ironically occupied by Brackley.

Following the win over Yeovil, Elliot said: “It was the first time we went into a match outside the relegation zone and showed the mentality and composure to go and get another three points

“I didn’t feel there was any apprehension in the team. The lads looked like the shackles were off.



“I said to the lads that you’ve got to make sure you get as many points on the board because going to Carlisle and then Scunthorpe, things could change.

“But I told them for the first time in a long time, this is in your hands now. So you don’t need to check the table, you don’t need to worry about anyone else. And I’m sure everyone will, because that’s normal, but now you win your games and you stay up.

“The big thing for me is that we look like a team that has the bit between our teeth, we’re buying into the structure and the shape.”

Gateshead travel to Carlisle on Good Friday before hosting Scunthorpe on Easter Monday.

They will conclude their season with trips to Aldershot and Altrincham, with a home match against Jermain Defoe’s Woking sandwiched in between.



And with the great escape nearly complete, Elliot and Co can dream of looking back towards those playoff places next term.

Football.title: Erling Haaland drops £100K at auction - and then immediately gives purchase away
Football.content:
Erling Haaland drops £100K at auction - and then immediately gives purchase away

Manchester City sharpshooter Erling Haaland won an auction before donating his prize and hopes he can inspire youngsters from his hometown to 'dream big'

View 2 Images Erling Haaland dropped a significant sum before making a kind gesture (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Erling Haaland has splashed out £100,000 at auction before immediately giving his purchase away. The Manchester City superstar spent the vast sum on a book before donating his home municipality of Time, in Norway.

‌



The striker picked up a unique edition of Snorre Sturlason's Royal Sagas from 1594, and made it the most expensive Norwegian book of all time after spending 1.3 million kroner. Haaland bought the book in December despite admitting to not being a big reader.

‌



"I have never been a big reader, but I want the book to always be open, so that you can read about those who came from my area, from Bryne and Jæren," Haaland said in a press release.

‌



"I've been lucky enough to live out my dream through football, and I know not everyone gets that chance. Books give so many more people the chance to dream big, see new possibilities and find their own path."

The book details the history of medieval Norse kings, with tales of Viking kings, queens, farmers and warriors. Per Haaland's wishes, it will be placed on permanent display at Time's local library.

The book was put up for auction by Johan Fredrik Odfjell, a Norwegian businessman and bibliophile, with Time Municipality only recently announcing that Haaland and his father Alfie made the purchase.

‌



The book is the only surviving copy of the two-volume 1594 manuscript and under the conditions of the donation, must be permanently displayed and made accessible to the public at the Bryne library.

“We are extremely grateful for this incredibly generous gift, said Andreas Vollsund, the mayor of Time Municipality. “Erling and Alfie are giving us the opportunity to do one of the most important things we can do for our young people: give them the joy of reading.”

Football.title: Eddie Howe under threat as Newcastle CEO speaks out after two-hour meeting
Football.content:
Eddie Howe under threat as Newcastle CEO speaks out after two-hour meeting

There has been some talk over the future of Eddie Howe with Newcastle sitting in 12th place in the Premier League table.

View 2 Images Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe has found himself under pressure this summer. (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

More doubt has been put on the long-term future of Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, with club chief David Hopkinson failing to offer any guarantees over the boss's future. Pressure increased on Howe following the 2-1 derby defeat against Sunderland in Newcastle's last outing.

‌



Hopkinson has now disclosed that he held a two-hour meeting with the manager in the immediate wake of the defeat at St James' Park. Newcastle's CEO outlined expectations from the club's hierarchy for the remaining seven fixtures of the 2025/26 season during interviews with journalists at St James' Park this week, where the club's latest financial figures were discussed.

‌



Newcastle announced impressive results, posting record revenues alongside a 44% surge in commercial income, as the club's turnover climbed by £15m to £335.3m - despite the absence of European football. Profit after tax came in at £34.7m.

‌



Thomas Tuchel admits mass international withdrawal of Arsenal stars looks 'suspicious' READ MORE :

With Champions League earnings from this season due to feature in next year's accounts, the financial picture will look even brighter in 12 months' time - though nobody at Newcastle needs reminding that failing to secure European football this term could significantly hamper the club's financial momentum.

That has led to the pressure on Howe continuing to mount, with the club stuck in 12th place in the Premier League table despite progressing to the last 16 of this season's Champions League. The spotlight on the head coach has grown more intense following the defeat in the Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland, and Hopkinson stopped short of offering any guarantees over Howe's long-term prospects. Instead, he stressed the importance of everyone at the club concentrating on the short-term, which includes challenging away fixtures against Crystal Palace, Arsenal and Nottingham Forest before the campaign draws to a close.

When quizzed about Howe's future, Hopkinson said: "I don't have a stance on his future. What I can tell you is that the derby loss hurt. We take it seriously. There's nothing within us that thinks 'well, it's just three points and on we go'. It has resonated.", reports Chronicle Live.

‌



"I spent a couple of hours in a one-on-one lunch recently with Eddie, and we talked through a multitude of things, including that.

"Eddie's our manager. I expect to have a great run to the end of the season here, and we'll talk about the future when it's time. Right now, we're focused on this season's competition."

Hopkinson was pressed on his comments regarding Howe and whether he had delivered an open-ended response. The chief executive, who reaffirmed the necessity of securing European football next season, backed by finance director Simon Capper seated beside him, said: "I would not frame it that way (open ended). We are not looking to make a change at the moment.

‌



"We are not having those conversations. We are still in the midst of the season. Right now we are focused on the seven matches we have remaining and not distracting ourselves with speculation about what we may or may not do in the summer.

"Right now, all of us have only got so much bandwidth and we are focused on this season and finishing strongly."

View 2 Images Newcastle United Chief Executive Officer David Hopkinson has failed to speak about the long term future of Eddie Howe. (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, both Capper and Hopkinson made clear that Newcastle must view themselves as a 'trading' club, acknowledging that financial regulations now make buying and selling an absolute necessity, and that Howe is fully aware of what lies ahead in the transfer market.

This comes amid mounting speculation surrounding the futures of several of Newcastle's high-profile players, with the likes of Sandro Tonali, Tino Livramento and Bruno Guimaraes all being linked with departures this summer.

Hopkinson said: "Eddie is experienced, thoughtful and understands squad cost management and the need to maximise our competitive opportunity. Eddie wants the exact same things we do and we have lots of good dialogue with him. What I can tell you is he is aligned and understands this."

‌



The club's financial results, meanwhile, highlighted the considerable progress made since the Saudi-led takeover in 2021, with substantial growth following years of stagnation under Mike Ashley. Hopkinson insists the figures place the Magpies in a strong position to realise their ambition of achieving 'world class' status by 2030, though the numbers were given a boost by selling the leasehold of St James' Park and other assets to a company that forms part of its wider operations.

A club statement read: "Newcastle United Limited has announced its financial results for the year ended June 2025, confirming record revenues and a 44% increase in commercial income as the club's operational transformation continues.

"The 2025 financial results are supported by success on the pitch during the account period, with the club winning a first domestic trophy in 70 years and achieving a fifth-place finish in the Premier League to qualify for the 2025/26 UEFA Champions League.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Despite not playing in European competition during the accounting period, the club's turnover rose by £15m to £335.3m. Profit after tax was strongly positive at £34.7m. A 44% rise in commercial revenue was a key driver in overcoming the loss of European earnings. This was supported by investment into a new in-house retail operation and the opening of the unique 'St. James' STACK' fan zone next to St. James' Park.

"The club also undertook the reorganisation of its property holdings and group structure to support future investment in infrastructure, which was accounted for in accordance with FRS102 accounting rules. The 2025 financial results reflect a profit on disposal of £133.2m, which will be slightly adjusted in Financial Year 2026 based on results of a now-concluded Premier League fair market value process."

‌



Hopkinson said in a club statement: "Our financial results reflect not only strong progress on and off the pitch, but also the firm foundations being laid for the future we all aspire to. Thanks to the continued backing of PIF and the Reuben family, we are better positioned than ever to invest in our long-term vision and create the conditions for sustained success.

"Together with our supporters, our staff, our players and our ownership, we move forward with ambition and a shared belief in what this club can become.

"As these results pre-date my arrival, I also want to express my sincere gratitude to Darren Eales for his leadership and dedication during an important period of transition for the club. He made a lasting contribution during a key phase, and we are building on that progress with confidence."

Football.title: Man Utd given Sandro Tonali encouragement as Newcastle CEO makes transfer admission
Football.content:
Man Utd given Sandro Tonali encouragement as Newcastle CEO makes transfer admission

Manchester United have been linked with a move for Newcastle and Italy star Sando Tonali as they look to strengthen their midfield this summer

View 2 Images Newcastle and Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali has been linked with Manchester United (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson has admitted the club will have to be open for business as Sandro Tonali continues to be linked with Manchester United. Several midfielders have been linked with a summer move to Old Trafford, with numerous players in that position expected to depart M16.

‌



The Red Devils are set to lose Casemiro when his contract expires at the end of June, and with Manuel Ugarte facing an uncertain future at Old Trafford amid his struggles, reinforcements will be needed. Nottingham Forest star Elliot Anderson, Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton and Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba have been among the names linked alongside Tonali.

‌



Colleagues at ChronicleLive have reported that Newcastle are calm regarding Tonali’s future at St James' Park. The 25-year-old has a contract that runs until 2029, with the option for another year.

‌



But speaking as the club’s accounts for the last financial year were released, Hopkinson has referenced Alexander Isak's sale to Liverpool last summer as an example of how the Magpies could sell their best players for the right price.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: “We haven’t got an overall strategy with regards to [moving] players out. We think through what players might or might not want to do this summer.

‌



"But if an Isak-like scenario presents itself again, any player under contract is going to leave on our terms and we’re going to maximise the opportunity that might represent for the club. That absolutely does (mean extracting the maximum price).

View 2 Images Sandro Tonali continues to be the subject of speculation (Image: PA)

“For me, Isak was a good sale (in terms of getting a British record fee). I wasn’t here for the Isak situation, so I don’t want to comment on something I didn’t see first-hand. What I do know is that players that leave this club will need to do so on our terms.”

‌



United's rivals, Manchester City, are also reportedly interested in Tonali. Meanwhile, sources at Premier League leaders Arsenal have confirmed that the Italian is not on their radar.

It is understood that Newcastle are frustrated with the player's agent, Giuseppe Riso, who has openly discussed the possibility of his client leaving. The agent has mentioned this summer's World Cup finals as an opportunity for Tonali to put himself in the shop window, although Italy still need to beat Bosnia and Herzegovina in a playoff on Tuesday evening to qualify.

‌



When previously speaking about the former AC Milan star to Italian media, he said: “If he shines at the World Cup, will City or Arsenal be hot on his heels?

“I don’t know, but it’s very likely. Everyone is waiting for the World Cup; then a thousand scenarios will unfold, but it all kicks off after the World Cup.”

United have also been linked with Tonali's Newcastle teammate, Bruno Guimaraes. However, it has been reported that the Italy international remains their top target over the Brazil star.

Football.title: German media warn Newcastle's Nick Woltemade over 'poor decisions' as spot at risk
Football.content:
German media warn Newcastle's Nick Woltemade over 'poor decisions' as spot at risk

German media have delivered their verdict on Newcastle United star Nick Woltemade ahead of the World Cup

View 2 Images Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade started for Germany on Monday (Image: Inaki Esnaola, Getty Images)

Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade featured for Germany on Monday evening but remains vulnerable to losing his position in the squad ahead of World Cup 2026. Julian Nagelsmann's team secured a 2-1 victory over Ghana.

‌



The fixture held particular importance as it was Woltemade's final opportunity to turn out for his country before the pre-tournament squads are announced in May. The 24-year-old has established himself as a consistent starter for Germany, netting four times in six matches during World Cup qualifying and he completed 78 minutes in last night's friendly.

‌



However, Woltemade faces competition for his starting berth from Arsenal's Kai Havertz, who converted from the penalty spot against Ghana. His other rival, Stuttgart striker Deniz Undav, emerged as the match-winner after securing an 88th-minute goal at his home stadium.

‌



Woltemade's recent performances in a Newcastle shirt will hardly alleviate the pressure, having gone 13 league games without finding the net. Here is what the German press made of Woltemade's display.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Kicker

A match report from Kicker highlighted the "intensity" that the Newcastle forward has delivered to the German national setup. Woltemade was included in the starting XI on his return to Stuttgart's ground after appearing as a substitute in a 4-3 triumph over Switzerland last week.

‌



Newcastle make decisions over £125m transfer disappointments with new signing lined up READ MORE :

Alan Shearer involved in bike crash as Newcastle and England icon shares health update READ MORE :

He set up Liverpool's Florian Wirtz for a goal that was disallowed for offside and nearly notched his fifth international strike with a shot that rattled the crossbar early in the second period. Woltemade's combination play formed a key element of his performance but he also faced criticism for "making a few poor decisions".

Summarising Woltemade's prospects, Kicker wrote: "In the striker hierarchy, a healthy and fit Kai Havertz, this time deployed on the right and scoring from the penalty spot, is ahead of Woltemade."

Bild

Bild focused on Woltemade and Undav's contrasting fortunes. The Newcastle striker was reported to have squandered a "golden opportunity" in the opening stages with a shot that sailed wide of the goal.

‌



Germany goalscorer Undav is enjoying a rich vein of form for Stuttgart. His decisive strike against Ghana prompted Bild to acknowledge that "things aren't going quite so well" for Woltemade.

The match report stated: "Will Nagelsmann stick with his current strategy of making Undav the number three forward behind Havertz and Woltemade? Nagelsmann has 75 days until the World Cup opener against Curacao to find the answer."

View 2 Images Woltemade hit the woodwork with a header against Ghana (Image: Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images)

‌



Suddeutsche Zeitung

The German outlet challenged Nagelsmann's choice to field Woltemade from the start but also provided some reassurance as to why he might feature at the World Cup. The formation saw Havertz shifted out to the right flank to make room for the Newcastle player in a central position.

Suddeutsche Zeitung wrote of the manager's team selection: "If the starting line-up sent a message, it was this: Nagelsmann can't be all that enamoured with the running patterns of Deniz Undav, Germany's most prolific striker." Woltemade was tellingly chosen ahead of Undav at his own stadium.

He sent "an excellent chance just wide" within four minutes and was "applauded enthusiastically" after subsequently striking the woodwork. Crucially for Woltemade, Havertz "seemed perfectly at ease" playing on the wing, which might reduce his competition for the central striker role.

Football.title: Thomas Tuchel admits mass international withdrawal of Arsenal stars looks 'suspicious'
Football.content:
Thomas Tuchel admits mass international withdrawal of Arsenal stars looks 'suspicious'

England stars Eberechi Eze, Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are four of ELEVEN Arsenal players to have pulled out of international duty

View 2 Images Tuchel spoke before England's clash against Japan (Image: 2026 The FA)

England boss Thomas Tuchel has admitted the fact that 11 Arsenal players have withdrawn from international duty looks 'suspicious', but insists there are no doubts over the honesty of the quartet of Three Lions stars to pull out.

‌



Eberechi Eze withdrew before Friday's 1-1 draw against Uruguay, while Noni Madueke limped out of that clash and has returned to Arsenal. Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka did not join camp until Saturday but were both sent back to the Gunners after medical tests.

‌



They join Martin Odegaard, Leandro Trossard, William Saliba, Gabriel, Jurrien Tumber, Piero Hancapie and Martin Zubimendi in withdrawing from international duty.

‌



Arsenal are still competing on three fronts as they bid to end their long trophy drought and secure a first Premier League title for more than 20 years.

Elliot Anderson on sliding doors moment in England training and World Cup inspiration READ MORE :

They hold a nine-point lead over Manchester City in the title race, although the Blues have a game in hand and are still to play the Gunners at the Emirates.

City beat Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final before the international break, ending hopes of a quadruple for Mikel Arteta's side, while Pep Guardiola's men are already out of the Champions League.

‌



Arsenal travel to Southampton in the quarter-finals of the FA Cup on Saturday night while City face Liverpool earlier in the day in the last eight.

The Gunners then face a two-legged Champions League quarter-final against Sporting Lisbon and eyebrows have been raised at the number of international withdrawals given their packed fixture schedule.

But Tuchel insists there are no doubts over his players' honesty. "Everyone can do the math and it's a lot of players, of course," he said. "During the situation, it looks a bit suspicious but I can only talk for our players.

‌



View 2 Images Madueke limped out of England's clash against Uruguay (Image: Getty)

"I still have 100% trust in the honesty of Bukayo and Declan. We did medical tests. I saw them. I have no reason to believe that Declan is not honest with me. I have no reason to believe Bukayo is not honest.

"But given the amount of Arsenal players, I understand the look."

‌



The outlook on Madueke is more serious than his other Arsenal and England teammates, with Tuchel admitting he may face a prolonged spell on the sidelines.

"Noni is out for some days and maybe some weeks," he added. "Everybody will be out for quite some days but not dramatically. It's disappointing, but I'm not upset with the players, I'm not angry with the players.

"I got the feeling that everyone was desperate to come. Some of the injured players even stayed to start their treatment here. That just shows me they want to be around the group.

‌



"No one left straight away. Everyone stayed, had another dinner, had another night, had another breakfast, because it's a good spirit and that's how it should be.

"I’m not sure if I want to give the nature of the injuries away. I think Arsenal would not be happy but Declan feels a discomfort since quite a while, and he’s playing through it, and he’s just now on the edge. It’s the same with Bukayo.

‌



"He played in pain through the Carabao final and we could see that he had not the same impact that he wishes to have for his club against Man City.

"You can see it and he confirmed it straight away. He tried with treatment in the three days to get rid of it and be ready but it's just too much of pain. We will not push players now who are at 70 per cent through a friendly match."

England take on Japan this evening in their final friendly before jetting off to the USA. Jude Bellingham will miss the game as he recovers from a hamstring problem while Ben White may start after his goalscoring return to international action on Friday.

Football.title: Inside England's World Cup base with security concerns and scorching heat addressed
Football.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Inside England's World Cup base with security concerns and scorching heat addressed

Mirror Football brings you the exclusive ins and outs of England’s World Cup 2026 base, delivered by an MLS star who knows every blade of grass

View 4 Images Swope Soccer Village will be England's training base for the duration of the World Cup 2026 (Image: Getty Images for USSF)

The World Cup 2026 is fast approaching, with just 10 weeks left until Thomas Tuchel and his England squad take to the field in the United States, Canada and Mexico. Tuchel will be hoping to become the first manager to lead the Three Lions to World Cup glory since Sir Alf Ramsey lifted the Jules Rimet trophy on home turf in 1966.

‌



Despite this agonisingly long wait, the 2024 Euros finalists go into the tournament as one of the favourites, boasting a squad stacked with superstars. Given the expectation on both the players and staff this summer, the FA have been keen for England to have the best possible preparation before and during the tournament, with the squad set to clock up thousands of miles of air travel should they reach the final.

‌



One way in which they’ve tried to do so is by selecting Swope Soccer Village in Kansas City as their training base. The state-of-the-art facility is the home of Sporting Kansas City II - the development team for Major League Soccer side Sporting Kansas City. It is not too far away from England’s cosy hotel for the tournament, The Inn at Meadowbrook.

‌



Mirror Football - JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

England will have full use of the nine full-size pitches - six of which are synthetic turf and three of which are Bermuda grass fields - at the training ground, which can seat up to 1,500 fans.

A player who has come through SKC’s various youth teams to now face the likes of Lionel Messi in the MLS is right-back Jake Davis, who called Swope his home for several of his nine years with the club. As someone who knows the ins and outs of the training centre, Davis spoke to Mirror Football about exactly what England’s World Cup hopefuls can expect from their base of up to six weeks.

‌



“England will be in for a treat, especially with the people here and the facilities and what we have to offer,” the 24-year-old said.

Trent Alexander-Arnold told to forget World Cup spot as Thomas Tuchel actions say it all READ MORE :

“I've been at this club for nine years through all the levels. I've been a player at Swope. I've trained there for multiple years and luckily now I've moved to Compass Minerals. But I think the one thing that I'm grateful for about our club is - yes, our club has grown by itself, we were able to build a new training facility, and it's great for us - but what's special about Swope is it is a first-team facility. That's where we used to be.

“As a club for us to have two places where we can be, it's great. I think also for England whole are coming here, to utilise Swope, it's a first-team facility. It's tight knit and close quarters. It's nice and you’re close to your team-mates. The fields are amazing. I think that it's everything you need to perform at the top level.

‌



“Top teams can utilise everything you've got there and especially that it'll all be for one team, I think that you can utilise even more. When I was there, there were multiple teams, so for one to be able to take that over and make it theirs, they're enhancing everything it has to offer.”

First opened in 2007 and used by the likes of FC Kansas City in the National Women’s Soccer League in the past, Swope Soccer Village is located in the outskirts of Kansas City, in the US’ Midwest. England picked it as their training base due to its central proximity to their group stage fixture against Croatia in Texas, before they head to the Atlantic coast to face Ghana and Panama.

View 4 Images Jake Davis of Sporting Kansas City knows all about the training ground (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Being nestled away from the city centre allows Tuchel and his players to escape the fan frenzy of what has been described as the ‘soccer capital’ of America. But the private nature of the facility itself is another crucial reason why it was picked, preventing any outsiders from seeing the tactics and penalties they are working on in training.

Davis explained: “The field has walls or fences with tarps over it so no one can really just go pull up and watch at the facility. That would be a little bit crazy. Everything's secluded, everything's private. Even where the actual facility is, the location of it, it's away from the city. I wouldn't say it’s in the middle of nowhere but it's very secluded compared to where the first team here is at. So there's nothing to worry about in terms of privacy or what people may see.

“The facility itself is in a peaceful area. Aside from being on the pitch, I think there's a lot of open space. I don't know anyone on the England team. I don't know what the routines are. But there's not a lot of outside noise near the facility.

‌



“I think that, in terms of putting the blinders on, focusing on what you need to do and also taking a step away from the pressure of just being at the World Cup, the players and staff will have enough space and resources to be fully focused on soccer. But they'll also be able to take a step out of that and do their own thing. I wish I knew Thomas Tuchel and his habits but if pressure is mounting up, the area that it’s in is very good for outside of the game.”

View 4 Images The ground is home to Sporting Kansas City II in the second tier of US football (Image: NCAA Photos via Getty Images)

It has been revealed that the perimeter fences could be doubled in height to create an even more intimate atmosphere. The weight room inside Swope will be transformed into a players’ lounge for England’s stars to enjoy some downtime, with an outdoor gym being added outside for the players to soak up the sun. And there will be plenty of sun.

‌



One of the biggest concerns about England’s ability to go all the way this summer has not been the quality of their players or tactics but how well they can adapt to the sweltering US summertime heat. England will have to play in the low humidity, 27-31 degrees celsius heat while training in Kansas City, with similar temperatures expected for their fixtures in New Jersey and Boston.

Their opening game in Dallas will be the most gruelling, however, with very high humidity expected and a 32-37 degree temperature. An additional three-minute drinks break midway through each half will be introduced for that very reason, though that didn't make matters any less difficult at last summer’s Club World Cup.

View 4 Images Swope Soccer Village is based in a green and open area (Image: Swope Soccer Village)

‌



Speaking about potential challenges that may arise for England, Davis said: “The heat in America in general is different than what it is in different countries or different continents. Anywhere you are in America, in the summer, it's going to be hot. But it's nothing that no one's ever played in. Everyone can handle themselves and will adapt to that.

“Obviously, we saw it at the Club World Cup. It is going to be pretty similar to that. But it's the World Cup, there's more motivation to push through these things and those factors are big factors. I think, with the quality top teams like England and Argentina have and whoever will be in Kansas City or in the Midwest of America, they'll be able to strive through that.

“Listen, I'm not going to say it's not hot. It gets very hot. But you acclimatise to that."

Football.title: Dubois, Scotney and the future | 'The talent is phenomenal'
Football.content:
Elite world champions from Britain, like Caroline Dubois and Ellie Scotney, will showcase their talents on Sky Sports' stacked bill on Sunday.

There are promising signs too, thanks to the success of England boxing teams at Junior and Youth level, that a vibrant future beckons for the sport in the years to come.

Boxing is one of the country's most successful sports across its age groups, its strength told in the number of international medals being won.

Chris Connelly, head of performance at England Boxing, pointed out: "I think a perfect example is the Youth World championships in Colorado. It was Colorado, it's an expensive gig. We only took 10 boxers and we finished with eight World champions.

"One got a bronze that could have easily got through to the final on another day and only one didn't medal. Nine medals out of 10, eight of them being Youth World champions, I think India finished below us and they had double the amount of boxers than us.

"The last four major competitions we've been to, three Europeans and a Youth Worlds, Schools, Junior, Youth Europeans and a Youth Worlds in that period, we were the top country in all of them. No 1 basically in the world."

He added: "It's a bit of a concerted effort with England that we don't take the full distribution of weight categories, one because we can't afford it. But you'll turn up and Ukraine and India will have every single weight category, and we're still outperforming them and topping that medal table, even though a lot of tournaments we're at, we've got half the amount of entrants as those countries."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports Boxing's Andy Scott runs though everything you need to know about Caroline Dubois' lightweight unification clash with Terri Harper, April 5.

England Boxing provide a pathway to GB, the Olympic squad, but enter international competitions in their own right at senior, youth and junior level.

"The clubs in England are unbelievable. We've got 1200 boxing clubs across England, just producing talent upon talent and then they come through our doors and similar to when we pass them on to GB I suppose, they come through our doors and we just try to harness them to go internationally and represent us well," Connelly said.

"If there's non-Olympic weights that are good enough to compete internationally we'll bring them on the senior programme," he added, with World silver medallist Emily Asquith a prime example of that.

"My job is that they leave England in a better place, whether that's to go to GB, whether that's to go professional. If they go professional it's still great for us, still great for boxing, it's still someone on the telly doing well that inspires someone else to go into an England Boxing club and then that cycle all starts again.

"They'll make a better pro because of the two years they've spent with us."

Image: Ruby White exemplifies the success of young England teams (Pic courtesy of USA Boxing)

Whether they find their way into the pro ranks or to the Olympic Games, the future of British boxing is looking bright.

"The talent is phenomenal. Alice Pomphrey we passed over to GB, she was a Youth World champion. Ruby White is just an incredible talent," Connelly said.

"Ruby has won the last four major competitions she's been to. She's won the last three European championships and the Youth World championships.

"She's the real deal."

At the recent U19 World Boxing Futures Cup in Thailand, Lily Bassett won a superb gold medal for England, defeating five world-class opponents en route to the top of the podium.

Jaya Kalsi also impressed, securing bronze after four demanding bouts in Bangkok. Four of the squad are now ranked inside the top five U19 boxers in the world.

All six of the selected squad are now eligible for the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal later this year.

Bassett, who's trained by her father James and head coach, and Gogglebox star, Marcus Luther, is also coming off an incredible run of winning three straight European gold medals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Caroline Dubois and Terri Harper shared an intense face-off and traded a few more words after the launch press conference for their fight on April 5.

The success of England boxing teams is an indicator that the future is bright for British boxing. Caroline Dubois and Ellie Scotney, long before they were professional world champions, represented England in different age groups. Dubois was a stunningly successful junior and youth, never losing in those categories and winning the Youth Olympics.

The strong foundations of the sport in this country are due to the amateur boxing clubs.

"Our big thing is those 1200 boxing clubs around the country and where they're located and who they cater for and how easy it is to just go into a boxing club and start the sport," Connelly said.

"The ABA, England Boxing's been around 150 years, but then we have a really robust regional and national championship structure that is open to anyone, if you're good enough."

Watch the Caroline Dubois-Terri Harper and Ellie Scotney-Mayelli Flores bill live on Sky Sports on Sunday April 5.

Football.title: ‘Unacceptable’ to not talk about periods in sport, says Panagarry
Football.content:
Periods remain the biggest barrier for secondary school age girls in accessing physical activity while at school, data from Youth Sport Trust shows.

But for Loughborough Lightning captain, Nat Panagarry, the fact that young girls now are experiencing the same worries as she did 20 years ago is "unacceptable".

Whether girls worry about leaking, cramps, bloating, or heavy bleeding, Panagarry is determined to change the narrative around the menstrual cycle in sport and stop girls from dropping out when they hit puberty.

"It does make me really sad because it feels like it was something that I was worrying about when I was 14/15 and I'm 35 now, we're 20 years on, and the young girls coming through are still having that feeling," she said.

"That conversation around periods isn't happening enough, it makes me sad and frustrated because I know how much joy sport has brought me.

"I think the person I am today is due to playing sport, the people I've met and the confidence it's given me.

"So to think that young girls that want to play sport still have that barrier of their period and feel like they can't speak about it, or don't know where to get female products from, or can't afford those products, that to me is just unacceptable.

"It is our duty, being older women, to be having these conversations so the next generation don't feel like this, it shouldn't be something that's stopping young girls hitting the hockey pitch or a tennis court or a cricket pitch or football pitch, anything."

Panagarry has played for Lightning since 2015, reaching 200 Netball Super League games on March 8, and in that time has seen the attitudes and research into women's sport change drastically - but she believes we're still not where we should be.

Image: Loughborough Lightning won the NSL Grand Final in 2021, 2023, and 2024

She revealed how in recent years Lightning's support staff have taken a lot of time to look into how women's health issues can impact them on the court, crediting this as a part of the reason for their consistent success.

But with that, she's realised how the norms she was raised on can be harmful, and that discussing your menstrual cycle with coaches and teammates doesn't make you any less strong.

It's also not just how we approach periods in sport, the Lightning captain is also passionate about seeing free menstrual products available in all women's public restrooms.

"It's been really nice to see conversations about the menstrual cycle being brought up more, with women and girls being more open to speak about it because so many of us are going through the same thing," Panagarry said.

"But for some reason I remember when I was younger it was such a taboo subject in sport and I always think being from Preston up north I had that 'no nonsense attitude, when you walk in you give a hundred per cent of whatever you've got' embedded in me.

"Now we're getting to that point where we're realising that that's not always possible and it isn't healthy, mentally you just can't give a hundred per cent, especially when you're going through your period."

A big worry for Panagarry used to be leaking, as she experiences heavy bleeding particularly in the first couple days of her cycle, and the options of shorts for under her netball dresses were always light colours, such as pink and purple.

To avoid leaking and try to give herself peace of mind while playing, she even used to wear both a pad and a tampon at the same time.

But now with black undershorts and the option of period underwear, from Lightning's sponsor Hustl, she feels so much more confident on the court.

She has also noticed that some of the younger players coming through are significantly more open to talking about periods than she was at their age, praising their unwavering confidence.

Football.title: Bartoli urges Raducanu to take a leaf out of Sabalenka's coaching manual
Football.content:
Former Wimbledon champion and Sky Sports analyst Marion Bartoli has urged Emma Raducanu to take a leaf out of Aryna Sabalenka's coaching manual by sticking with one coach for a long period of time.

Sabalenka has become the fifth woman in history to complete the 'Sunshine Double', beating Coco Gauff in the Miami Open final, two weeks after claiming the Indian Wells crown.

She has benefited immensely from having a stable team behind her, winning multiple Grand Slam titles and reaching world No 1.

The 27-year-old has been working alongside coach Anton Dubrov, a fellow Belarusian who has tasted success with her since 2020, fitness coach Jason Stacy, hitting partner Andrei Vasilevski, and fiance Georgios Frangulis.

The addition of Max Mirnyi, a former Grand Slam doubles and mixed doubles champion, has imparted his wisdom by adding some variety to her game since last August, particularly with the serve and volley.

Raducanu parted company with Francisco Roig in the wake of her second-round defeat at the Australian Open.

She enjoyed a strong run of form while working with Andy Murray's former coach Mark Petchey early in 2025 in a temporary arrangement, but hired Roig in August as she sought a new permanent coach.

Following a six-month spell in which she endured disappointing results, Roig, who formerly coached Rafael Nadal, became the ninth coach to depart since Raducanu's 2021 US Open win, with the pair gelling well on a personal level but not aligning on style of play.

Her next tournament in Romania saw her reach her first final since her victory in New York in 2021, and since the split from Roig, Raducanu insisted she is happy working with hitting partner Alexis Canter, a 27-year-old British former player who reached a career-high ranking of 779 last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Raducanu reflected on her loss to Amanda Anisimova at Indian Wells

Raducanu retained Canter as part of her set-up, as well as working with Petchey at Indian Wells. She is next due to appear at the Upper Austria Ladies Linz, which takes place from April 6-12, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

Speaking in Miami, Bartoli said: "For Emma to keep changing coaches is a difficult topic because you need to have some sort of stability.

"When you look at the coaching system, Sabalenka has had the same coach for such a long period of time and I think for Emma it's about trying to find the right fit!"

Bartoli added: "I do strongly believe she will need to find someone she can trust for a long period of time if she wants to improve."

Martina Navratilova, an 18-time Grand Slam champion, has called on Raducanu to pick her next coach carefully and most importantly - give them time.

"I mean, I don't know what's the record for a coach - maybe six months! So, I wish that she would really pick whoever she wants to be her coach carefully and then stick with it," said the former world No 1.

"Give it a year because it takes a while to be comfortable with making changes and being able to incorporate the person into your game.

"The biggest thing I see I think she could get fitter which the coach has nothing to do with, but you know, the coach can only do so much.

"Pick the right coach and stick with him or her, please!"

I do strongly believe she will need to find someone she can trust for a long period of time if she wants to improve.

Henman: Raducanu needs more physical resilience

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Tim Henman and Martina Navratilova debate if Raducanu needs to commit to a long-term coach and improve her off-court physicality to reach her full potential

Sky Sports analyst Henman thinks Raducanu should concentrate on working on her physicality to match the likes of fellow Grand Slam champions Sabalenka, Iga Swiatek, Elena Rybakina and Coco Gauff.

The four-time Wimbledon semi-finalist said: "It was highlighted in a match against (Amanda) Anisimova.

"She's never going to be as big a ball striker as Anisimova and the physicality that she brings to the court is obviously intimidating, as these top players are. But that's where I think Raducanu needs to be physically stronger. She needs more physical resilience so she doesn't get the little injuries that put her away from the court. They stop her building the momentum on the match court.

"You can still do a lot of physical work on the court, whether it's two on one when you're hitting and moving and building up that physical resilience to get stronger, to get faster, to hit the ball harder, to serve bigger. If I could pinpoint one area, it would most definitely be fitness."

Emma Raducanu's NINE coaches

Nigel Sears



Best known for coaching former top five players Amanda Coetzer, Daniela Hantuchova, Anett Kontaveit and Ana Ivanovic, Sears joined her team in April 2021 and oversaw her incredible breakthrough run to the Wimbledon fourth round.



Andrew Richardson



Guided Raducanu to her historic Grand Slam title at the US Open as a qualifier. Raducanu opted not to extend his trial contract immediately after the victory.



Torben Beltz



Angelique Kerber's former coach lasted only five months. They split in April 2022 with Raducanu transitioning towards a new training model involving LTA coaching support.



Dmitry Tursunov



Raducanu took on the former pro on a trial basis during the summer of 2022 but Tursunov decided not to continue, later citing red flags in her camp that he felt could not be ignored for a long-term commitment.



Sebastian Sachs



The German joined in late 2022 but the partnership was cut short when Raducanu required multiple surgeries, leading to a mutual split.



Nick Cavaday



The 14-month stint was her longest professional partnership, helping her return to the top 60 before he stepped down in early 2025 due to personal health issues.



Vlado Platenik



Hired on a trial basis in March 2025, the partnership lasted only 14 days.



Mark Petchey



Andy Murray's former coach provided crucial tactical knowledge through Wimbledon where she went out to world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka, despite an encouraging display.



Francisco Roig



Appointed in August 2025, Rafael Nadal's former mentor offered elite tactical clarity, but after her Australian Open exit in January 2026, Raducanu announced their split.



'The spotlight will never dim'

Football.title: Mekies 'confident' Red Bull can give Verstappen faster car
Football.content:
Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies is "confident" the team can give Max Verstappen a faster car for the remainder of the Formula 1 season.

Verstappen is considering walking away from the sport due to his dissatisfaction with Formula 1's new regulations but has also not been able to fight at the sharp end of the field.

For the first time since 2017, Verstappen has gone three consecutive races without finishing in the top five and his latest disappointment came at Suzuka on Saturday where he was knocked out in Q2, before recovering to eighth in the race.

Due to the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix, there are no F1 races in April, so Mekies is hopeful Red Bull will make "a very good step forward" for the next round in Miami in early May.

"We need the time to simulate back what we see in the data into the tunnel, into our simulator, try some sensitivities and all of that we can do without racing," said Mekies.

"Does it mean you come to Miami and you have solved everything as a miracle? No, but again, am I confident that the team will get to the bottom of that understanding and start bringing improvements already in Miami. That's what we will see but only the track and the lap time will give us an indication on whether we go into the right directions.

"I don't think we should expect miracles about the amplitude of closing the gap because the is substantial but what we would like to see is to have a car where our drivers can push again, measure a gap to competitions in these conditions when we are able to push and then the rest will be pure development to the end of the year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A look at Max Verstappen's disappointing start to the 2026 Formula 1 season

Verstappen: Current Red Bull pace is not sustainable

Red Bull are sixth in the Constructors' Championship while Verstappen is only ninth in the Drivers' Championship, having fought for a record-equalling fifth straight drivers' title last year.

The Dutchman spent most of the Japanese Grand Prix battling Alpine's Pierre Gasly for seventh but felt he was unable to get by due to the battery deployment regulations.

Verstappen stated he was "trying to hang on" during the race as the car balance was "unpredictable" in a similar fashion to qualifying, where he was bumped out in Q2 by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen's nightmare start to the season continued as he was knocked out of Q2 at the Japanese Grand Prix

"This is not sustainable for us as a team. We need to work hard to understand our problems and bring improvements," he told Sky Sports F1.

"You can have a bad balance but that doesn't take away how we have to race. I commented on that already a few times. That is a limitation. A lot of drivers are speaking out on it. That's the biggest one for me.

"Of course I would like to win, but I can also accept if I'm driving P7. The way I'm driving, P7 with the systems, is not a lot of fun."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen urged Red Bull performance improvement during the upcoming break ahead of the next race in Miami

Mekies said he has had "zero discussions" with Verstappen over the four-time world champion's future in F1, despite his frustrations.

"We have a lot of work to do. I'm sure by the time we give him a fast car, he will be a much happier Max," he said.

"By the time we give him a car he can push and make the difference with, he will also be a happier Max. Honestly that's 100 per cent of our discussions right now.

"As per the regulations, they are coming with some good aspects and more tricky aspects and as a sport, with the other teams, we will meet in the break to see how we can tweak them to make things better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen says his Red Bull is extremely tough to drive and Jacques Villeneuve thinks it's down to its unpredictability

Mekies: Red Bull one second slower than Mercedes

Red Bull expected a challenging 2026 as they have built their own power unit, in collaboration with Ford, for the first time. However, it appears to be the chassis and aerodynamics which are the biggest problem for Verstappen, rather than engine performance.

Verstappen crashed in the first qualifying of the year in Australia but came through the field from 20th to sixth, while Isack Hadjar had qualified third, so there were encouraging signs at Red Bull.

But they scored no points in the China Sprint weekend with Verstappen retiring from the Grand Prix due to a coolant failure and continued to struggle with starts too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Verstappen crashed into the barriers during Q1 at the Australian Grand Prix

Asked where the potential Red Bull had in Australia had gone, Mekies said: "We certainly think that in China we made a step back and we measure that not only against the top guys but also against the midfield that got closer to us, so in China we for sure made a step back.

"I don't think it's a product of the number of corners only. There's a layer where in certain cornering speed and cornering conditions we lose some performance compared to what our package is supposed to give us, so this we need to work on.

"It was a touch better in Japan compared to China, especially in the race. We didn't see it because we were again a distant fourth [best team] and it doesn't interest anyone to be a distant fourth. But the overall gap is what we have been talking about, it's about one second to the best guys and half a second to the best Ferraris is probably where we are at."
